_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the input file x17-rd-input.json; I opened no other repository file, did no search and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: ALPS via the edelweiss flower of the Alps, SOUND via the song in The Sound of Music (itself set in the Austrian Alps), so both sides click and reinforce each other.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; true and lines are accurate.

hints.reason: FIRST via Eve as the first woman, APPLE via the forbidden fruit traditionally pictured as an apple; the line correctly notes Genesis never names the fruit.

pairs.pair_note: ADAM (first man, Adam's apple) is an equally good alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: BACK via the instantly familiar compound quarterback, FOOTBALL via the game's four quarters (and the quarterback itself), so both sides are solid.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, easy phrase-join with a second true link to football.

hints.reason: BALL via the Wilson sports-ball brand, FRIEND via Wilson the volleyball companion in Cast Away; a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Top-tier hint.

hints.reason: BEAR via Paddington Bear, LONDON via the London station he is named after and the city he lives in; easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate lines (from 'darkest Peru', named after Paddington station).

hints.reason: BIG via the name Big Ben, LONDON via the landmark itself; very easy but clean, and the bell-versus-tower detail is stated correctly.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; fine as a gentle clue.

hints.reason: BLOCK via Minecraft's block-built worlds, DIAMOND via the prized diamond ore; both are core, widely known features.

pairs.pair_note: Solid modern pop-culture hint.

hints.reason: BOAT via the gravy boat, THANKSGIVING via gravy as a dinner staple; the two sides meet on the same table, which makes it satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that earns its place because both halves are the same scene.

hints.reason: BOOT via Italy's boot-shaped map outline, PIZZA via pizza's Neapolitan origin; classic and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean.

hints.reason: BRIDGE and TROLL both via Three Billy Goats Gruff, where the troll lives under the bridge; the bare word GRUFF makes the player recall the tale, which is a nice aha.
hints.fix: TROLL line: "In Three Billy Goats Gruff, the troll under the bridge threatens to gobble the goats up."

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect hint; TROLL line should name the tale so it links the hint, not just the scene.

hints.reason: BUS via the film Speed and its bomb-rigged bus, LIGHT via the speed of light; a crisp two-sense hint.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the 50 mph line is accurate.

hints.reason: CAMP via the camp counselor, LAWYER via counselor (at law); a genuine double meaning with a pleasant click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning.

hints.reason: CAP and FEATHER both via the Yankee Doodle lyric about sticking a feather in his cap and calling it macaroni; surprising word, instant recall once seen.
hints.fix: FEATHER line: "Yankee Doodle sticks a feather in his cap and calls it macaroni, slang for a fashionable dandy."

pairs.pair_note: Delightful; the FEATHER line asserts that the feather itself is what he called macaroni, which is one reading of an ambiguous 'it', so soften it.

hints.reason: CASE via cracking (solving) a case, EGG via cracking an egg; clear, familiar double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair.

hints.reason: RED via the matador's iconic red cape, CHARGE via the charging bull; the line nicely corrects the color myth.

pairs.pair_note: Good scene hint; 'a matador's cape is red' is a fair shorthand for the red muleta.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via the midnight deadline, DRESS via her ball gown turning back to rags at midnight; DRESS is reached through the story rather than directly, and PUMPKIN would compete if on the board.

pairs.pair_note: Sound and accurate, but the DRESS side is the weaker half; watch for other Cinderella words (PUMPKIN, SLIPPER, COACH) on the same board.

hints.reason: CLOSET and SKELETON together via the idiom 'skeleton in the closet', whose meaning is a hidden secret (closet alone also means secret, as in a closet fan).

pairs.pair_note: Hint names the idiom's meaning; fair and familiar.

hints.reason: COLOR via Holi as the festival of colors with thrown colored powder, INDIA via Holi as a major Indian festival; widely known in the U.S. through color runs and media.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate familiarity but fair and accurate.

hints.reason: COW via steer as cattle, TURN via to steer; a clean double meaning, and the line carefully avoids calling a steer a cow.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and fair.

hints.reason: DANCE via the hula as a Hawaiian dance, GRASS via the grass skirt; the 'often pictured' wording keeps it accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, accurate.

hints.reason: DEER via doe as a female deer, NOTE via 'Doe, a deer' standing for do in Do-Re-Mi; a lovely aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: DISNEY via Walt Disney World near Orlando, MAGIC via the NBA's Orlando Magic; a satisfying place-plus-team link.

pairs.pair_note: Lines say 'near Orlando', which is accurate.

hints.reason: DOLL via the voodoo doll, PIN via the pins stuck into it; instantly familiar, and the text correctly frames it as a pop-culture trope.

pairs.pair_note: Route is sound; mild sensitivity because the trope misrepresents a real religion (Vodou), so owner may want a PG/sensitivity call.

hints.reason: VIRUS via viral as the adjective form of virus (near-giveaway), DRESS via the 2015 'The Dress' meme, which many will recall only after the explanation; facts are true but one side is trivial and the other takes effort.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate but lopsided; VIRAL is almost the target word itself, and the DRESS route rests on a meme that is fading.

hints.reason: EGG via Humpty Dumpty usually drawn as an egg, FALL via his great fall; the 'usually pictured' wording is accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and accurate.

hints.reason: FAMILY via Vin Diesel's family-first Dom Toretto meme, FUEL via diesel fuel; a fun pop-culture double meaning.
hints.fix: FUEL line: "Diesel is a fuel used by trucks, buses and some cars."

pairs.pair_note: Great hint; 'many cars' overstates diesel use in U.S. cars, so soften to 'some'.

hints.reason: FATHER via Vader revealing he is Luke's father, SKY via the surname Skywalker; both are iconic Star Wars knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the FATHER line avoids the famous misquote.

hints.reason: FILM via the Oscars, TRASH via Oscar the Grouch's trash can; a classic two-sense name.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: FOX via Nick Wilde the fox, FLASH via the slow DMV sloth named Flash; the sloth scene is the film's most famous gag and the ironic name gives a real payoff, though players must recall the name.

pairs.pair_note: Character-name recall is the risk; I judge Flash familiar enough (heavily memed, sequel in 2025) but a second opinion is welcome.

hints.reason: ROBIN via the name Robin Hood, FOX via Disney's 1973 Robin Hood drawn as a fox; widely known animated classic.

pairs.pair_note: Good; note ROBIN appears in three pairs in this batch (HOOD, WILLIAMS, POOR), so avoid putting them on one board.

hints.reason: ROBIN via the first name of Robin Williams, GENIE via his famous voice role in Aladdin; a warm, satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: SWITZERLAND via Heidi's Swiss Alps setting, GOAT via Peter the goatherd and the goats she tends with him; classic and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Fair classic-literature hint.

hints.reason: GUITAR via the guitar pick, TOOL via the pick or pickaxe; clear double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair.

hints.reason: ORDER via the phrase pecking order, HEN via hens pecking, the very behavior the term was coined from; the etymology makes it more than a bare phrase-join.

pairs.pair_note: Lines are accurate (the term comes from studies of hens).

hints.reason: HORN via French horn and TOAST via French toast, both instantly familiar, but it is a bare prefix join with no shared idea and FRENCH completes many other board words (fries, kiss, door, press), so the pairing is flat.

pairs.pair_note: Fair but unremarkable phrase-join; explanation ('both start with French') is true but adds nothing. Fine as filler if the owner wants easy clues.

hints.reason: STREAM via the Gulf Stream ocean current, JET via Gulfstream business jets; the same word splits into a brand and a current, a neat aha though the jet brand is only moderately familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Clever; JET and STREAM also form 'jet stream', which helps players see the pair.

hints.reason: LAKE via Swan Lake, SONG via swan song; both phrases are instantly familiar and the pairing is a satisfying classic.

pairs.pair_note: Good phrase-join.

hints.reason: LINK via the hero of The Legend of Zelda, SWORD via his Master Sword; widely known gaming reference with a small 'Link isn't Zelda' aha.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: TICKET via the lottery ticket, MILLIONAIRE via a jackpot making someone a millionaire; plain but clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, low delight; acceptable as a gentle clue.

hints.reason: NINJA via Leonardo of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, TITANIC via Leonardo DiCaprio; two famous Leonardos give a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: PENGUIN via Batman's villain the Penguin, UMBRELLA via the Penguin's signature trick umbrellas; UMBRELLA reaches Batman only through the Penguin, but that trait is widely known.
hints.fix: UMBRELLA line: "In Batman stories, the Penguin is known for his trick umbrellas."

pairs.pair_note: Fair chain; the UMBRELLA line should mention Batman so it connects the hint.

hints.reason: ROOM via escape room, PRISON via prison escape; both are instantly familiar and share the same idea of getting out.

pairs.pair_note: Good; better than BREAK (prison break, break room).

hints.fix: RICH line: "Poor is the opposite of rich, and Robin Hood robs the rich to help the poor."

pairs.pair_note: The current RICH line is garbled ('the people Robin Hood robs' dangles); ROBIN side needs the Hood step.

hints.reason: SAFE via the umpire's safe call, STRIKE via the umpire calling strikes; both are signature umpire calls.

pairs.pair_note: Clear and accurate.

hints.reason: SHAPE via oval as a shape (category link), WHITE via the Oval Office in the White House; a two-step but familiar route with a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: WHITE side is two hops (Oval Office, White House) but familiar.

hints.reason: SKYSCRAPER via being tall, STORY via a tall tale (tall story); the extra pun of a building's stories adds a nice payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Good layered hint.

hints.reason: TOOTH via a cavity in a tooth, SUGAR via sugar causing cavities; true and clear but a flat cause-and-effect link, and SWEET (sugar is sweet, sweet tooth) is clearly better.

pairs.pair_note: Replace with SWEET; CAVITY is acceptable but unremarkable next to it.
